annotations.annotation_text: Page 80 opens Book 1, Chapter 4 ("The Burial of HCE") during the Age of Gods (transition) phase. This passage continues the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history, featuring HCE, Mamalujo, Kate the Slop. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 80 ("The Burial of HCE"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods (transition) dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.

annotations.annotation_text: Issy/daughter figure "Issy" on page 80 ("The Burial of HCE"): the narcissistic mirror-daughter, modeled on Isolde and Swift's dual muses Stella and Vanessa, appears here within the burial of the giant in the landscape, the archaeological mound, the Four Annalists surveying history. Her prismatic splitting into twenty-eight Rainbow Girls reflects the cycle's Age of Gods (transition) phase through youthful seduction and self-reflection.
